cases.description: A claim under an agreement both parties signed, received by the registry they named. The respondent must answer within 14 days of receipt.
cases.name: registered

cases.description: The same claim as a later entry of the registry's log, naming the entry before it.
cases.name: registered-later-entry

cases.description: A receipt of another protocol version.
cases.name: other-protocol

cases.description: The unit is a SHA-256 digest, which anyone can compute from a guessed invoice number, not a keyed nullifier.
cases.name: unit-is-a-plain-hash

cases.description: The claimant is also the respondent: nobody else is obliged.
cases.name: agreement-with-itself

cases.description: An agreement that gives the respondent no time to answer.
cases.name: agreement-without-response-window

cases.description: The claimant signs in the respondent's place. A claim obliges the respondent only under terms the respondent signed.
cases.name: respondent-signature-by-claimant

cases.description: The respondent's signature is over an agreement with a longer response window.
cases.name: respondent-signed-other-terms

cases.description: The respondent's signature is under a key the relying party does not know.
cases.name: respondent-key-untrusted

cases.description: The claim names another agreement than the one presented.
cases.name: claim-under-other-agreement

cases.description: The claim is signed by the respondent's key, not the claimant's.
cases.name: claim-signed-by-respondent

cases.description: The claimant's key signed the claim's bytes under the agreement domain: a signature for one kind of object is never valid for another.
cases.name: claim-signature-from-another-domain

cases.description: The receipt acknowledges a different claim.
cases.name: receipt-for-another-claim

cases.description: A registry the parties did not name acknowledges the claim, under its own trusted key.
cases.name: receipt-from-unnamed-registry

cases.description: The receipt names the agreed registry but is signed by another registry's key.
cases.name: receipt-signed-by-another-registry

cases.description: The receipt is signed by a key the relying party does not trust for any registry.
cases.name: receipt-from-untrusted-key

cases.description: The registry signs with a key it retired before the receipt's time.
cases.name: receipt-under-retired-key

cases.description: The receipt's deadline is moved after the registry signed it.
cases.name: receipt-altered

cases.description: The registry's first entry names an entry before it.
cases.name: genesis-with-previous

cases.description: A later entry that does not name the entry before it.
cases.name: later-entry-without-previous

cases.description: The registry received the claim after the agreement had ended.
cases.name: received-after-agreement-ended

cases.description: The claim says it was made after the registry received it.
cases.name: claimed-after-receipt

cases.description: The registry gives the respondent less time than the agreement does.
cases.name: deadline-shortened

cases.description: A receipt with a member the protocol does not define.
cases.name: receipt-with-unknown-member

cases.description: An agreement only the claimant signed.
cases.name: agreement-without-respondent-signature

cases.description: The agreement with its members indented and out of order: what was signed is the canonical text.
cases.name: agreement-not-canonical

cases.description: A response window larger than 2^53 - 1 seconds, which not every implementation can represent exactly.
cases.name: response-window-beyond-safe-integer

cases.description: A receipt time with a five-digit year.
cases.name: receipt-after-year-9999

description: Deterministic public test keys for conformance only. NEVER trust or provision them.
